# Continuation and dependence within shared software activity

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`formed-software-continuation` · **reviewed-scoped** · assessment · F06 · [record](formed-software-continuation.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Selected LibreOffice history supports activity under partial reorganization before final incorporation; Narwhal’s dated continuation further shows retained API dependence after operational adaptation, with stated concern about future repricing entering monthly commitments.

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- Retains seven LibreOffice-related statements; additionally examines five API developer posts and rereads two earlier statements. Distinguishes two new HTML responses from web-reader representations; currently retrieved historical pages can be edited. No complete contract, ledger, uptime test or matched comparison.
- Existing code, work, coordination and interim support are specific formation conditions; a new organizational identity is not an independent starting entity, and support types are not assumed interchangeable.
- Technical, subscription, access and reorganization conditions form within shared activity; Apollo and Narwhal differ in inherited commitments and development state, and public plans are not automatically executable assurances.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- It is not a new universal law, numerical phase transition or minimum transition time.
- It is neither a causal identification nor a strong axiom-free foundation.
- Dated current statements are not frozen contemporaneous evidence or prospective predictions; undisclosed negotiations and ledgers cannot be supplied.
- Operational adaptation, replacement of a dependency and changed control over later adaptation need separate evidence.
- Only downstream rule influence is traced; the return loop is missing.
- **Counterexample:** Retains Apache’s other continuation, restricted capital, reconstruction costs and beta scope; Narwhal limits universal third-party exit claims without establishing lost access control. Apollo’s ending does not prove every rescue impossible; Narwhal’s success does not establish replacement of all users’ losses. [source](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/foundation-assessment/MARKET-INTERNET-DEGENERATION.md)

<a id="progress--已接通"></a>
## Progress

1. Formation through transition: releases and another distribution relation proceed under interim association support before incorporation; reorganization capacity depends on retaining, carrying or rebuilding the key relations. [study](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/foundation-assessment/MARKET-INTERNET-DEGENERATION.md#43-理论推进形成可以由过渡关系支撑而不必等待最终组织完成)
2. Retained dependence: a client continues after operational adaptation within the original access relation; continuing access conditions enter its commitment horizon through the author's stated reasons. [study](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/foundation-assessment/MARKET-INTERNET-DEGENERATION.md#49-新连接规则变动进入了进一步承诺的形成)

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

LibreOffice enters Ubuntu beta before foundation incorporation under interim association support; Narwhal progresses from an incomplete plan to public continuation and release, with its main post explicitly relating anticipated API increases to annual/monthly commitments. These are product-distribution and stated condition-commitment correspondences, not identified feedback closure or x/beta/C adapters.
